page.description: Flatcar Container Linux editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: An immutable, minimal Linux distribution designed exclusively for running container workloads on bare metal and in cloud environments. No package manager, no filesystem drift, automated atomic updates via Google-style update mechanism.
pros: Immutability eliminates configuration drift; filesystem is read-only
Automated, atomic, canary-style updates with rollback support
Minimal attack surface with only container runtime tools
Proven at scale by companies like Adobe (18,000+ nodes), Giant Swarm, Equinix
cons: No traditional desktop or general-purpose use; containers only
No package manager — software must be baked into custom images or delivered as containers
No signed ISO image available; only container tarball and raw disk images are shipped
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for Flatcar Container Linux; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the container tarball to a target and boot from an ignition config, or deploy via cloud-init with an Ignition user-data file. Not a traditional bootable USB image.
